title: Offline bootstrap policy and dependency minimization for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Ava Thompson
description: PRD: Define an operational policy and concrete acceptance criteria for 'offline bootstrap' (air-gapped or minimal-egress VPC) that minimizes external dependencies required during initial cluster/operator bootstrap and subsequent control-plane upgrades. This ticket captures requirements, success metrics, allowed egress patterns, artifact distribution options (mirror, physical media), image provenance validation, and fallback plans for staged upgrades. It focuses on reducing the number of external endpoints operators rely on during provisioning and upgrades so customers with strict network controls can adopt Private deployments with predictable upgrade windows.
goals: Define minimal external dependencies for bootstrap and upgrade (DNS, time sync, CRL lists)
Spec out allowed egress flows and a default 'proxyless' operator mode
Define artifact distribution options and acceptance criteria for mirror-based and physical-media bootstraps
Specify operator behavior during partial connectivity and automated rollback triggers
Establish verification steps, telemetry signals, and runbook links for on-call and customer support
non_goals: Full implementation of mirror sync tooling (engineering task)
Replacing customer-specific airgap policies — instead provide a recommended default
On-prem hardware procurement or physical logistics (handled by customer)
requirements: Operator must support a 'minimal-egress' mode configurable at install time (boolean flag)
Bootstrap must succeed with only mirror endpoint(s) and package signatures, or via local image registry provided by customer
Upgrade controller must validate image signatures before pulling when egress is allowed
Operator must expose preflight checks that enumerate required egress targets and expected ports
Operator must behave idempotently: partial artifact sync must not leave the cluster in an unrecoverable state
Telemetry must emit a 'bootstrap.progress' event with stage and last-reachable-endpoint; alerts configured for >30m stall during bootstrap
acceptance_criteria: Preflight: Running the operator preflight against a simulated isolated VPC (no internet) must surface a checklist of missing artifacts and a deterministic remediation path
Mirror-only bootstrap: Given a configured local mirror registry (no outbound internet), a fresh install completes and all images pass signature validation

Staged upgrade with partial egress: If the control-plane loses access to an external mirror mid-upgrade, operator pauses rollout and creates a rollback plan; test demonstrates safe rollback without pod-level data loss
Physical‑media fallback: Provide an operator-run checklist for installing from transported artifacts (OCI tarball) and confirm install/upgrade completion in a sandbox runbook
Minimal telemetry: Bootstrap emits progress events and a failing-stage alert within 30 minutes, verified in staging telemetry dashboard

Operatorless-exit: Customers can configure 'operatorless' runtime mode where runtime nodes continue serving while control plane is offline for up to configured SLA (e.g., 6 hours) without requiring egress
Security: All downloaded artifacts have valid signatures and provenance metadata; manual override requires RBAC approval and is audited
Documentation: Confluence PRD, runbook, and a one-page 10-step install checklist exist and link to example mirror configs and iptables/nftables allowlists
notes: 2025-02-15: Initial draft PRD created during PM kickoff with Infra and Security. Decision to prioritize 'dependency minimization' rather than building bespoke mirror tooling.
2025-02-18: Engineering triage: ENG recommends 'minimal-egress' flag and a preflight API endpoint (see ENG-1842). Estimate 5 points for scoping and acceptance tests.
2025-02-24: Security review requested; asked to verify KMS/HSM interaction when images are pulled from mirrors (security_review_required=true).
2025-02-27: Design input: UX for installer flags and post-install diagnostics (console modal with checklist) accepted; follow-up design ticket DES-901 upcoming.
2025-03-01: Trade-off discussion: full offline artifact sync vs. on-demand mirror pull — agreed to support both, deliver mirror-first path for MVP and document physical-media fallback.
2025-03-02: Added acceptance criterion for operator idempotency and telemetry signals after reliability team pointed to incident IN-2024-11 as a reference.
